newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia welcomes aid, pledges prudent policies.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia welcomes aid, pledges prudent policies.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto on Friday welcomed $5.3 billion in aid pledges by the Consultative Group for Indonesia (CGI) and said the country would use it responsibly.

"We are happy that the world still trusts us as proved by this aid. We accept this international aid with a full sense of responsibility, which means we will use this aid responsibly," Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad quoted Suharto as saying following a meeting with the president.

The CGI, comprising 18 donor countries and international organisations including Japan, the United States, the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank (ADB), pledged $5.3 billion in aid to Indonesia in Tokyo on Thursday.
The aid was pledged at the 1997 donors' conference on July 17 for disbursement over the next 12 months.
The CGI pledged $5.26 billion in aid to Indonesia in 1996.

The World Bank pledged $1.5 billion for 1997 compared with $1.2 billion in 1996 and Japan offered $1.87 billion compared with $1.91 billion in 1996. The ADB's $1.2 billion was unchanged from last year.
Mar'ie said the aid would be used mainly to build infrastructure, boost human development resources and eradicate poverty.
He said the CGI had praised Indonesia's macro-economic policies and Indonesia would continue to follow such policies.
"Our economic fundamentals are good. We will continue to implement prudent economic policies," Mar'ie said.
He said Indonesia was had recently repaid some $3.5 billion in foreign debt.
"We are in the process of paying off another $1 billion at this moment," he said. He declined to give further details.
Indonesia's overall foreign debt is currently more than $100 billion.
